items.stem: Why do cardiac muscles never tire, unlike skeletal muscles?
items.answer: Cardiac muscle is specialised for rhythmic contraction and relaxation throughout life, with many mitochondria and a rich blood supply.

items.stem: Why do plant cells not burst in fresh water, while animal cells may?
items.answer: The rigid cell wall of plant cells resists the pressure of water entering; animal cells have only a thin, flexible membrane.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: rigid wall. 1 mark: no wall in animal cells.

items.stem: Why does a population of bacteria grow very fast?
items.answer: Each bacterium divides into two by binary fission in a short time, so numbers double every generation.

items.stem: Can an object have constant speed but changing velocity? Give an example.
items.answer: Yes. If its direction changes, velocity changes even at constant speed, e.g. a car going round a circular track at steady speed.

items.stem: Classify as a suspension or a true solution: flour in water, sand in water, sugar in water, muddy water, soda water.

items.stem: Ball A (0.1 kg) moving at 6 m/s hits ball B (0.2 kg) moving at 2 m/s along the same line. After the collision A moves at 0 m/s in its original direction (negative means reversed). Find the velocity of B.
items.answer: 5 m/s
items.markingKey: m₁u₁ + m₂u₂ = m₁v₁ + m₂v₂ ⇒ 0.1×6 + 0.2×2 = 0.1×0 + 0.2v₂ ⇒ v₂ = 5 m/s.

items.stem: A house in Indore uses an electric iron of 1000 W for 0.5 h a day and 5 LED bulbs of 10 W each for 6 h a day. Find the electricity used in 30 days in kWh and the cost at ₹6 per unit.

items.stem: Distinguish between smooth (unstriated) muscle and cardiac muscle on the basis of structure, control and location.
items.answer: Smooth (unstriated) muscle: involuntary, spindle-shaped, uninucleate cells without bands; found in walls of the stomach, intestine and blood vessels. Cardiac muscle: involuntary, cylindrical, branched, uninucleate cells that contract rhythmically throughout life; found in heart.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each: structure, voluntary/involuntary control, location.

items.stem: A bat emits ultrasound of frequency 100 kHz in air (v = 340 m/s). Find the wavelength in millimetres, and explain why humans cannot hear it.

items.stem:

(i) Is the motion uniform or non-uniform? (ii) What is the acceleration? (iii) Find the speed at t = 4 s. (iv) Find the distance covered in these 4 s.
items.answer: (i) Non-uniform (uniformly accelerated). (ii) 3 m/s². (iii) 12 m/s. (iv) 24 m.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each: (iii) v = u + at; (iv) s = ut + ½at² = 0 × 4 + ½ × 3 × 4² = 24 m.

items.stem:

(i) In which beakers will the path of light be visible? (ii) Which mixture will settle on standing? (iii) Find the mass by mass % of salt in A. (iv) Classify A, B and C.
items.answer: (i) B and C (C shows the Tyndall effect; B scatters too, but settles). (ii) B. (iii) 25/175 × 100 = 14.3%. (iv) A: true solution; B: suspension; C: colloid.

items.stem: Classify the plant kingdom into its five groups. Give the distinguishing features and one example of each, and explain cryptogams and phanerogams.
items.answer: Thallophyta: undifferentiated, algae (Spirogyra). Bryophyta: no vascular tissue, amphibians (moss). Pteridophyta: vascular, no seeds (fern). Gymnosperms: naked seeds (pine). Angiosperms: seeds in fruits (mango). Cryptogams: hidden reproductive organs, no seeds (first three); phanerogams: seed plants (last two).
items.markingKey: 3 marks groups; 2 marks cryptogams/phanerogams.

items.stem: State the law of conservation of mass and the law of constant proportions. Write the postulates of Dalton's atomic theory and show which postulate explains each law.
items.answer: Conservation: mass is neither created nor destroyed in a reaction. Constant proportions: a compound always has elements in a fixed ratio by mass. Dalton: matter of atoms; atoms indivisible and indestructible (explains conservation); atoms of an element identical in mass and properties; atoms of different elements differ; atoms combine in small whole-number ratios (explains constant proportions); relative number and kinds of atoms are constant in a compound.
items.markingKey: 2 marks laws; 2 marks postulates; 1 mark linking.

items.stem: State Newton's three laws of motion with one everyday example of each. A force of 5 N gives a mass m₁ an acceleration of 10 m/s² and a mass m₂ an acceleration of 20 m/s². What acceleration will it give if both masses are tied together?
items.answer: First: object stays at rest or uniform motion unless an unbalanced force acts (passengers jerk forward on braking). Second: F = ma / rate of change of momentum (catching a ball by pulling hands back). Third: equal and opposite reaction on different bodies (recoil of a gun). m₁ = 0.5 kg, m₂ = 0.25 kg; a = 5/0.75 = 6.67 m/s².
items.markingKey: 3 marks laws with examples; 2 marks numerical.

items.stem: What are the changes seen in boys and girls at puberty? Name the hormones responsible and explain the importance of a balanced diet, hygiene and physical exercise during adolescence.
items.answer: Increase in height, growth of hair, voice changes (larynx grows in boys), active sweat and oil glands, development of sex organs; breasts in girls, facial hair in boys. items.stem: What are the causes and effects of air and water pollution? Suggest ways to prevent each.

Water: sewage, industrial effluents, fertilisers; effects – diseases, eutrophication, fish death; prevention – sewage treatment, effluent treatment, controlled fertiliser use.
items.markingKey: 2 marks air; 2 marks water; 1 mark prevention.

items.stem: What is ultrasound? Explain how SONAR works and derive the formula for depth. Write three other uses of ultrasound.
items.answer: Sound above 20 kHz. SONAR has a transmitter that sends an ultrasonic pulse and a detector that receives its reflection; if the echo returns after t, the pulse travels 2d, so 2d = vt and d = vt/2. Uses: cleaning hard-to-reach parts, detecting cracks in metals, echocardiography, ultrasonography, breaking kidney stones.
items.markingKey: 1 mark definition; 2 marks working and formula; 2 marks uses.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "An animal whose body temperature changes with the surroundings, such as fish, amphibians and reptiles."
items.answer: a cold-blooded animal
items.markingKey: (b) A cold-blooded animal is an animal whose body temperature changes with the surroundings, such as fish, amphibians and reptiles.

items.stem: Which of the following is a pure substance?
items.answer: mercury
items.markingKey: (d) Mercury is a pure substance. The others: soil – a mixture; wood – a mixture; sea water – a mixture.

items.stem: Earthquake-prone areas in India include:
items.answer: Kashmir, Uttarakhand, the North-East and the Rann of Kutch
items.markingKey: (d) Kashmir, Uttarakhand, the North-East and the Rann of Kutch.
options: Kashmir, Uttarakhand, the North-East and the Rann of Kutch

items.stem: Friction can be reduced by:
items.answer: using lubricants and ball bearings
items.markingKey: (c) using lubricants and ball bearings.

items.stem: The electronic configuration of phosphorus (atomic number 15) is:
items.markingKey: (a) K, L, M shells hold at most 2, 8, 8 (in this range): P = 2, 8, 5.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "A solution outside the cell with a lower water concentration than the cell, so the cell loses water."
items.answer: a hypertonic solution
items.markingKey: (a) A hypertonic solution is a solution outside the cell with a lower water concentration than the cell, so the cell loses water.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "The direction towards the centre of the circle in circular motion."
items.answer: centripetal direction
items.markingKey: (a) Centripetal direction is the direction towards the centre of the circle in circular motion.

items.stem: Which term is described here? "The male reproductive part of a flower, made of anther and filament."
items.answer: the stamen
items.markingKey: (b) The stamen is the male reproductive part of a flower, made of anther and filament.

items.stem: Which of the following is an object possessing kinetic energy?
items.answer: wind turning a windmill
items.markingKey: (b) Wind turning a windmill is an object possessing kinetic energy. The others: a wound-up spring of a toy car – an object possessing potential energy; a stretched rubber band – an object possessing potential energy; water stored in a dam – an object possessing potential energy.
options: a wound-up spring of a toy car

items.stem: The law of constant proportions was stated by:
items.answer: Joseph Proust
items.markingKey: (b) Joseph Proust.

items.stem: A boy shouts towards a fort wall in Jaipur and hears the echo after 3 s. How far is the reflecting surface? (speed of sound = 344 m/s)
Which type of muscle is found in the heart?
items.answer: cardiac muscle
items.markingKey: (d) Cardiac muscle: involuntary, cylindrical, branched, uninucleate cells that contract rhythmically throughout life.

items.stem: Define the scientific name.
items.answer: The internationally accepted two-word name of an organism, the same in all languages
items.markingKey: (b) The internationally accepted two-word name of an organism, the same in all languages. 1 mark: The scientific name – the internationally accepted two-word name of an organism, the same in all languages.

The system of naming an organism with two words, the genus name followed by the species name

items.stem: Which of the following is a chemical change?
items.answer: burning of a candle wick
items.markingKey: (c) Burning of a candle wick is a chemical change. The others: tearing paper – a physical change; melting of ice – a physical change; chopping wood – a physical change.

items.stem: Which of these is an example of a flood?
items.answer: Kerala floods 2018
items.markingKey: (d) Kerala floods 2018 is an example of a flood. The others: Bhuj, Gujarat 2001 – an example of a earthquake; Wayanad, Kerala 2024 – an example of a landslide; Kedarnath, Uttarakhand 2013 – an example of a landslide.

items.stem: When you jump from a boat to the shore, the boat moves:
items.answer: backward
items.markingKey: (d) backward.

items.stem: Why do we hear the sound of an approaching train earlier by putting an ear to the rail?
items.answer: Sound travels much faster in solids (steel) than in air, so it reaches the ear through the rail first.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: faster in solids. 1 mark: reaches earlier.

items.stem: Why is sclerenchyma called a dead tissue, and what is its function?
items.answer: Its cells are dead with walls thickened by lignin and almost no internal space; it gives strength and hardness.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: dead/lignin. 1 mark: strength.

items.stem: Why are birds and mammals called warm-blooded?
items.answer: They maintain a constant body temperature regardless of the surrounding temperature.
items.markingKey: 2 marks.

items.stem: Is the dissolving of salt in water a physical or a chemical change? Justify.
items.answer: Physical: no new substance forms; salt can be recovered by evaporating the water.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: physical. 1 mark: recoverable/no new substance.

items.stem: Harpreet's father drives 40 km a day for 30 days a month in Lucknow. If his car emits 200 g of CO₂ per km, how much CO₂ does it give out in a month, and in a year? About how many trees would be needed to absorb a year's emission if one tree absorbs 22 kg a year?
items.answer: 240 kg a month; 2880 kg a year; at least 131 trees.
items.markingKey: Month: 40 × 30 × 200 g = 240 kg. Year: × 12 = 2880 kg. Trees: 2880/22 ≈ 130.9, so at least 131 trees.

items.stem: Why do vehicles have crumple zones and airbags?
items.answer: They increase the time over which the momentum of passengers changes in a collision, reducing the force on them.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: increase time. 1 mark: reduce force.

items.stem: An element has the electronic configuration 2, 8, 5. Identify the element, its atomic number and whether it is a metal or a non-metal.
items.answer: Phosphorus (P), Z = 15, a non-metal.
items.markingKey: Total electrons = 15 = atomic number; phosphorus. (1 mark each part)

items.stem: Sahil's family drives 120 km (Lucknow to Kanpur) at 40 km/h and returns the same distance at 60 km/h. Find the average speed for the whole trip.
items.answer: 48 km/h
items.markingKey: Time = 120/40 + 120/60 = 5 h; average speed = total distance ÷ total time = 240 ÷ 5 = 48 km/h (not the mean of the speeds).

items.stem: Aarav studies a frog spawn of 3000 eggs in a village pond near Nashik. If only 10% of the eggs survive to become adult frogs, how many frogs develop? Why does the frog need to lay so many eggs?
items.answer: 300 frogs; fertilisation and development are external, so most eggs and tadpoles are lost.
items.markingKey: 10% of 3000 = 300. External fertilisation and no parental protection mean heavy losses.

items.stem: A ball is dropped from 5 m and bounces back to 3.2 m. What fraction of its energy is lost on the bounce, and where does it go?
items.answer: Energy is proportional to height: lost = (5 − 3.2)/5 = 0.36, i.e. 36%; it turns into heat and sound at impact.
items.markingKey: 1 mark: proportional to height. 1 mark: 36%. 1 mark: heat and sound.

items.stem: Two sounds of 500 Hz and 2000 Hz travel through air (v = 340 m/s). Find both wavelengths and state which sound has the higher pitch.
items.answer: 0.68 m and 0.17 m; the 2000 Hz sound has the higher pitch.
items.markingKey: λ = v/f: 340/500 = 0.68 m; 340/2000 = 0.17 m. Higher frequency, higher pitch.

items.stem: Describe, step by step, how you would separate a mixture of sand, camphor and common salt.
items.answer: Sublime camphor by heating; dissolve the rest in water and filter out sand; evaporate to get salt.
items.markingKey: 1 mark per correct step in a correct order (3 marks).

items.stem: Yash's father drives 20 km a day for 26 days a month in Lucknow. If his car emits 180 g of CO₂ per km, how much CO₂ does it give out in a month, and in a year? About how many trees would be needed to absorb a year's emission if one tree absorbs 22 kg a year?
items.answer: 93.6 kg a month; 1123.2 kg a year; at least 52 trees.
items.markingKey: Month: 20 × 26 × 180 g = 93.6 kg. Year: × 12 = 1123.2 kg. Trees: 1123.2/22 ≈ 51.1, so at least 52 trees.

items.stem:
Read: An element has 17 protons and 18 neutrons in its nucleus.
(i) What are its atomic number and mass number? (ii) Write its electronic configuration. (iii) What is its valency? (iv) Name the element and write the symbol with A and Z.
items.answer: (i) Z = 17, A = 35. (ii) 2, 8, 7. (iii) 1. (iv) Chlorine: Cl with A = 35, Z = 17.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem:
Read: Kunal cycles around a circular park of radius 105 m at a steady speed, taking 66 s for each round.
(i) Find the distance covered in one round (π = 22/7). (ii) Find the speed. (iii) What is the displacement after one complete round? (iv) Is Kunal accelerating? Explain.
items.answer: (i) 660 m. (ii) 10 m/s. (iii) Zero. (iv) Yes, the direction of motion keeps changing, so velocity changes.
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem:
Read: At a construction site in Gurugram, a crane lifts a 1500 kg slab of concrete to the 45 m high floor in 60 s at steady speed.
(i) Find the work done against gravity. (ii) Find the power of the crane. (iii) How much potential energy does the slab gain? (iv) If the crane's motor is 80% efficient, what electrical power does it draw? (g = 10 m/s²)
items.markingKey: 1 mark each part.

items.stem: Define mole and Avogadro's number. Calculate (a) the number of moles in 52 g of helium (He = 4), (b) the mass of 0.5 mol of water, (c) the number of molecules in 8 g of oxygen gas.
items.answer: Mole: amount with 6.022 × 10²³ particles; Avogadro number 6.022 × 10²³. (a) 52/4 = 13 mol. (b) 0.5 × 18 = 9 g. (c) 8/32 = 0.25 mol × 6.022 × 10²³ = 1.5055 × 10²³ molecules.
items.markingKey: 2 marks definitions; 1 mark each calculation.

items.stem: What is meant by a longitudinal wave? Describe with a diagram how sound travels as compressions and rarefactions in air. Define wavelength, frequency, amplitude and time period, and write the relation between speed, frequency and wavelength.
items.answer: A wave where particles vibrate parallel to the direction of travel. A vibrating object pushes air forward forming a compression (high density) and moving back forms a rarefaction (low density); these travel outward. Wavelength: distance between two consecutive compressions; frequency: oscillations per second (Hz); amplitude: maximum disturbance from the mean; time period T = 1/f. v = fλ.
items.markingKey: 1 mark definition; 2 marks propagation; 1 mark terms; 1 mark relation.

items.stem: Name the four types of animal tissues. Describe the structure, location and function of any two types of connective tissue and the three types of muscle tissue.
items.answer: Epithelial, connective, muscular, nervous. Connective: blood (fluid matrix plasma, RBC/WBC/platelets; transport), bone (hard matrix of calcium and phosphorus; support), cartilage, tendon, ligament, adipose. Muscles: striated (voluntary, limbs), smooth (involuntary, gut walls), cardiac (involuntary, branched, heart).
items.markingKey: 1 mark: four types; 2 marks: connective tissues; 2 marks: muscles.
